what: SSR Mining is a precious-metals miner with operations in the United States, Canada, Türkiye and Argentina. It produces gold at Marigold in Nevada, Cripple Creek & Victor in Colorado, which it bought from Newmont in 2025, and Seabee in Saskatchewan, and silver at Puna in Argentina. Its largest mine, Çöpler in Türkiye, has been suspended since a deadly heap leach slide in February 2024.
customers: Refiners and bullion buyers worldwide; the company is a price taker selling gold and silver at market prices.
money: Open-pit heap leach gold mines in Nevada and Colorado.
Silver and lead-zinc concentrates from Jujuy, Argentina.
Turkish gold mine halted since the February 2024 accident.
moat: Miners have little pricing power, so the moat is in assets: long-life, low-cost ounces in safe jurisdictions. The Cripple Creek & Victor acquisition added one of the largest gold mines in the US at a low price, and the company has a large cash balance. The Çöpler accident badly damaged its standing in Türkiye.
risks: The Çöpler accident killed nine workers; the restart timing, fines and remediation costs remain uncertain.
Earnings depend almost entirely on gold and silver prices, which are near record highs.
Losses of $98M in 2023 and $261M in 2024 show how quickly a single mine can swing results.
Argentina and Türkiye bring currency, tax and political risk.
Heap leach mines need constant reinvestment and can suffer grade and recovery shortfalls.
opportunities: Net income recovered to $396M in 2025 and the shares trade at about 7 times trailing earnings and 3.8 times EV/EBITDA.
Cash of $1.6B gives it room to fund growth and buybacks.
A successful Çöpler restart would add a large source of production that the market is giving little value.
Cripple Creek & Victor lifts production in a top-tier US jurisdiction.
watch: Çöpler restart decisions by Turkish authorities, gold and silver prices, cost per ounce at Cripple Creek & Victor, and capital returns.
view: SSR Mining trades like a company the market does not trust, and for good reason. The Çöpler slide in February 2024 killed nine workers and closed what had been its biggest mine, and the company lost $261M that year. The discount since then reflects not just lost ounces but doubts about management and about how Türkiye will treat the company. That discount is the opportunity, if you believe the rest of the portfolio is solid.

And the rest of the portfolio has improved. Buying Cripple Creek & Victor from Newmont added a large US mine cheaply, and with gold near record prices, net income came back to $396M in 2025 and $252M over the trailing period. The stock trades at about 7 times earnings and under 4 times EV/EBITDA, with $1.6B of cash. Strip out any value for Çöpler and the shares still look inexpensive at today’s metal prices.

The investment turns on two things you cannot control: the gold price and Turkish politics. A Çöpler restart would be a large re-rating catalyst; a permanent closure is mostly priced in. The bigger risk is that you are buying a miner at the top of the gold cycle, when every producer looks cheap. I think the stock is fairly cheap rather than mispriced, and this is a position to size as a leveraged gold bet with an option on Türkiye.
bull: Gold stays high, Cripple Creek & Victor performs and Çöpler restarts, adding production the market currently values at zero.
bear: Gold falls from record levels, US mine costs disappoint and Çöpler stays shut, leaving a mid-tier miner with shrinking production.
